captions.detailed: This 3D model features a matte black bicycle front-end assembly, consisting of a gravel bike fork and drop handlebars. The fork has a vertical tapered steerer tube branching into two flared-out blade legs, terminating in small metallic dropouts. At the top of the steerer, a short rectangular stem clamps onto the tube and extends forward to clamp a set of flared drop handlebars. The stem can rotate horizontally relative to the fork on a revolute joint, while the handlebars can rotate vertically within the stem clamp on another revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Generate a 3D model of a matte black gravel bike fork and handlebar assembly in CadQuery. The model should feature a tapered fork with two flared legs, a short blocky stem clamped to the top of the steerer tube, and flared drop handlebars. Implement revolute joints allowing the stem to rotate on the steerer tube and the handlebars to rotate within the stem clamp.
captions.factory: The assembly is constructed from three main parts: the fork, the stem, and the handlebars. The fork's steerer tube is modeled using a cylinder, and the legs are created by sweeping or lofting profiles to form flared-out blade geometries, complete with small cylinder-based dropouts at the tips. The stem is built using a combination of box primitives for the clamps and body, joined with cylindrical cutouts for the steerer and handlebar bores. The handlebars are modeled using a 3D wire path swept with a circular profile to form the flared drops. Finally, two revolute articulations are defined: one around the Z-axis connecting the stem to the fork, and one around the X-axis connecting the handlebars to the stem.
